goals: Mechanistic: characterize how peak SWE varies across the Wenatchee elevation gradient
Validation: quantify model peak-SWE skill against the 5 in-domain SNOTEL stations

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM simulates SWE (H2OSNO) natively and outputs it by default; NLDAS-2 forcing varies precip/temperature orographically with elevation, so an elevation-stratified column set resolves the peak-SWE gradient and supports SNOTEL comparison.

answerable: Peak SWE vs elevation gradient at 12 km resolution (NLDAS-2 orographic precip/temp variation)
Peak-SWE skill vs SNOTEL SWE at the 5 stations (co-located comparison)
Rain-snow transition elevation and its interannual variability

not_answerable.aspect: Sub-12 km sharpness of the high-elevation / ridgetop SWE peak
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 0.125deg has no within-cell lapse rate; a 12 km cell averages over surrounding lower terrain, systematically underestimating ridgetop SWE

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified by elevation band with light within-band replication
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 elevation bands spanning the 187-2870 m gradient x ~3 columns/band captures the SWE-elevation curve including the sensitive rain-snow transition, plus within-band spread from aspect/soil, without a blind dense grid.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Oversample the rain-snow transition (~1000-1700 m) where peak SWE is most sensitive to precipitation phase and the gradient is steepest; anchor endpoints in the valley and alpine bands to bound the curve.
sampling_strategy.replication: ~3 columns per band to expose within-band variability driven by distinct NLDAS cells, aspect and soil.

sampling_plan.reason: Bounds the low end where little to no seasonal snowpack forms; establishes the rain-dominated baseline.
Captures the onset of seasonal snow accumulation and high phase sensitivity.
Steepest part of the SWE-elevation curve; where most SNOTEL stations sit and peak SWE grows fastest.
Bounds the high end and tests the expected ridgetop SWE underestimation from 12 km forcing.

validation_design.comparison: co-located - place a validation column at each SNOTEL station and compare modeled vs observed annual peak SWE and its date over the overlapping years
validation_design.metric: bias, RMSE, correlation on annual peak SWE; secondary: melt-out date bias

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (multi-year window overlapping SNOTEL record), native SSURGO soil per column

requires_capabilities.why: NLDAS-2 12 km cells cannot resolve within-cell terrain, biasing ridgetop/alpine SWE low
requires_capabilities.blocks: Sub-grid sharpness of the high-elevation SWE peak

requires_capabilities.why: Needed to align modeled H2OSNO with observed station time series and compute peak-SWE metrics
Peak SWE is interannually variable; need several years overlapping the SNOTEL record
requires_capabilities.blocks: Robust gradient characterization and skill estimate

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM / elevation-band sampling + HUC boundary resolver
requires_capabilities.why: Downstream expander must place columns by elevation band within HUC 17020011
requires_capabilities.blocks: Turning the stratification rules into concrete columns

assumptions: Wenatchee (HUC 17020011) is within CONUS, so NLDAS-2 forcing (elevation-resolved) applies rather than Qian T62.
The 5 SNOTEL stations lie within the basin and report SWE over years within 1980-2018.
Peak SWE does not require multi-year spin-up (fast seasonal state); a short warm-up plus multi-year forcing suffices.
SSURGO soil is available per column; snow response is dominated by forcing phase, not soil, so soil is left native rather than controlled.
open_questions: What are the elevations of the 5 SNOTEL stations, so validation columns land in the correct bands and the ridgetop-bias check is targeted?
Which multi-year window best overlaps the SNOTEL records for all 5 stations?
Is aspect a meaningful secondary driver worth adding to within-band replication, or is elevation alone sufficient for this question?
